identifications.release: Nuxeo Web UI 3.1.19-rc.0 Go module source zip

evidence: forager downloads of both submitted branch archives from codeload.github.com matched the supplied SHA-256 hashes exactly; provenance sidecars are in scratch/nuxeo-review.
All 799 files shared by the release zip and the upstream v3.1.19-rc.0 tag are byte-identical. The upstream tar additionally has two vendored Handsontable files omitted from the module zip.
Independent atomscan purl scan of maintenance-3.0.x resolved SHA-256 4f72aabe65adcf4573253a08f2a04c965c485cc4b7abb850ec800338a575d9d7, identical to the forager-recovered branch archive.

The root preinstall changes from packages/nuxeo-web-ui-ftest to the sibling designer catalog then plugin/a11y. All three paths stay within the source repository. Bare npm install/ci resolves their declared dependencies; the child postinstall hooks only run check-engine --ignore.

Build scripts merge local i18n JSON into .tmp, copy vendored assets and bundle the Polymer UI. The functional-test runner spawns the bundled WebDriver test command and removes old test reports. Chrome-driver helpers run Chrome --version and fetch driver-version text from Google.

The 3D loaders decode Base64 model buffers and create shader-name regular expressions with eval. The designer catalog evaluates parsed boolean/number default expressions for component metadata. These operations remain detected as notable capabilities.

CI reusable workflow references account for the three fetched branches. Secrets authenticate npm/Maven/marketplace publishing, Crowdin translation sync and GitHub release operations. The newer reminder script uses the configured GitHub token only for GitHub GraphQL and sends PR-review summaries to a configured Teams webhook.

The highest-probability ML member in all four scans is the identical index.jsp. It chooses a repository base URL, generates a UUID nonce, updates the response CSP, and renders UI markup and local scripts; it has no operator-command dispatch, credential export or payload loader.
changes: Relocate six generic npm/yarn/pnpm pre/postinstall command atoms, the nested bare-install atom, and their OR group from supply-chain objectives to micro-behaviors/os/package-manager/hook-install. The operation owns the neutral observation; lifecycle phase is in IDs and manifest-path scope. Generic package installation does not prove a trust violation.

Keep all eight match conditions, exclusions, file/platform scope and confidence values unchanged. Six generic command atoms and their group become notable; the already-notable nested-install atom stays notable. Remove T1195 from the generic OR group because command declarations do not establish compromise.
Update exact attack consumers and retain the old objective-directory selection in Windsurf MCP configuration co-occurrence through explicit references to the moved group and nested-install atom.
Add notable preinstall npm ci, JSP CSP response-header setting and JSP Java UUID generation. No sample-name or dependent-package exceptions are added.
Clarify that the src-tree observation identifies JavaScript/TypeScript source: embedded JavaScript in a JSP can satisfy the file-type scope without making the container a .js file.

verification.focused_cases: 38 positive and near-miss cases in check.py plus three nested-postinstall controls passed.
verification.positive_fixture: void-elements@0.1.1 was fetched and its complete manifest/pre-install.js inspected. The two hostile consumers (cleartext module rebuild and install-then-local-node) and the suspicious dependency/source-rewrite findings remain before/after.
verification.stale_test: The original rules already did not classify cd ./lib && npm install evil && cd ../.. as a consumer-project escape. Correct the old test to require the named-dependency and install-command observations without a false escape conviction.
verification.detection_losses: None after mapping relocated IDs. The before/after comparison includes all analyzed archive members, not only outer summaries.
verification.scan_options: atomscan --no-update --analyze local --follow=none --mode slow --format json; fetched branches reviewed independently, including the maintenance-3.0.x PURL before and after.

remaining_disagreement: All four scans remain ML HOSTILE. The maximum member probability rises from 0.74479413 to 0.8505027 after accurate neutral JSP capabilities are added. This is a classifier false positive, not a reason to suppress supported behavior. The runtime deployment and all possible transitive dependency versions are not supplied; no hostile deployment is inferred.
